intended_object: For a K-algebra R and a matrix s in SL_n(R), the K-algebra homomorphism K[SL_n] = K[x_ij, det⁻¹]/(det − 1) → R sending x_ij ↦ s_ij. This is evaluation at an R-point, one direction of the Yoneda correspondence SL_n(R) ≅ Hom_K-alg(K[SL_n], R). Inferred from the docstring and from its use as the forward map of specialLinearGroupMulEquivAlgHom.
explanation: The coordinate ring is the GL_n coordinate ring K[x_ij][det⁻¹] (`Localization.Away (determinant K n)`) modulo the ideal `(det(matrix) − 1)`. `evaluate g` is the localization lift of `MvPolynomial.aeval (fun ij ↦ g ij.1 ij.2)`, so it sends x_ij to g_ij. The definition applies this to `toGL s` and descends to the quotient with `Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ`. The proof of descent is correct: an element m·(det − 1) maps to evaluate(m)·(det s − 1) = 0 because det s = 1. So this is exactly the evaluation homomorphism at s. The library proves it is a two-sided inverse of `specialLinearToSL`. The setting is fully general: K is any commutative ring, R any K-algebra, and n any finite index type with decidable equality (finiteness is needed for the determinant). I found no Mathlib counterpart: this Mathlib version has `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup` and the Hopf/Spec machinery, but no SL_n coordinate ring with its point equivalence. Strictly, this is a component of the point equivalence rather than a standalone notion, but the map it defines is standard and correctly formalized.
